channel.title: Hui Ning · Blog
channel.description: Thoughts on life, attention, AI, and biological design.

item.title: One life. What follows?
item.description: A finite life makes me want to choose my direction more carefully and worry less about passing judgments.

item.title: Choosing where my attention goes
item.description: There is more worth knowing than I can give serious thought to. I want to choose both my inputs and the questions I stay with.

item.title: Leave context for tomorrow’s self
item.description: How do I keep a long project moving? AI context management has made me reconsider the role of notes and reflection.

item.title: Forming a judgment I can stand behind
item.description: Different people and models offer perspectives. I still want to understand the reasons, examine the evidence, and decide how to act.

item.title: How I get agents to finish the work
item.description: Clear goals, sustained execution, and independent review help turn an agent conversation into work that can be inspected.

item.title: AI4Bio: What evidence comes after a prediction?
item.description: I want to understand where scaling improves a biological task, and how that improvement carries into measurable function and new conditions.

item.title: AI as intellectual leverage
item.description: AI gives more people a practical path from an idea to something useful. The better we understand a problem, the more we can ask of the tools.

item.title: Intelligence needs agency
item.description: Agency means carrying a goal through action, evidence, and revision until there is a useful result.

item.title: From encoded function to realized function
item.description: A biological design becomes useful through the whole path from encoded instructions to function in its intended setting.
